definition.interpretation: The successful execution of multi-tier sorting (accuracy 1.0) suggests that recursive task decomposition, even without explicit supervision, maintains operational integrity while introducing hierarchical structure. This supports the hypothesis that intelligent processes can generate complexity through internal branching logic.
definition.limitations: The experiment is restricted to sorting tasks; structural complexity growth may differ in non-sorting, state-dependent environments.
definition.next_step: Test scaling behavior with broader, non-linear task dependencies to determine if correctness persists across less structured recursive trees.

definition.next_experiment: Design a branching-logic experiment that introduces conditional task failures to observe how recursive processes handle entropy.
definition.reason: Initial sorting tests validate the mechanism of delegation; expansion to diverse task types is required to establish generalizability.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to maintain operational correctness or complexity growth metrics as task tree depth increases beyond current parameters.
definition.uncertainty: Whether this delegation-based complexity scaling holds for non-sorting, state-dependent tasks remains untested.

proposal.summary: Interpretation of recent hierarchical sorting experiments confirming complexity scaling through multi-tier task delegation.
proposal.title: WAKE Research Progress: Complexity Scaling Interpretation
